#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1

# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
#
# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
#
# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.

# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
zbuild_pg_resolve() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _child _self
    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_child"
        return 0
    fi
    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
    #
    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
    # about.
    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_pid"
    fi
}

# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
#
# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
    # as an option.
    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
    done
    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
_zbuild_pg_grace() {
    local _g="${1:-1}"
    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
}

# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
#
# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
#
# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
}

# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
#
# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
#
# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
#
# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
#
# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
zbuild_pg_register() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
    local _start
    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
zbuild_pg_kill() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
zbuild_pid_kill() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"

# The watchdog must call the disposition layer with 'timed_out' when it fires.
# Check lifecycle.sh and disposition-writing helpers used from within lifecycle.sh.
_timed_out_found=0
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi
# Also check that the runner or a helper wires the watchdog result to timed_out
_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi

if [[ "$_timed_out_found" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path" \
        "'timed_out' not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — timeout result cannot produce the required disposition"
fi

# After the change: the timed_out event must name the stage and the limit.
# The requirement says "ends with disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit".
# Check that the emit_event call for plugin.run.timed_out in lifecycle.sh carries
# both stage= and timeout_s= fields.
_timed_out_event_ctx=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _timed_out_event_ctx="$(grep -A4 'plugin\.run\.timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'stage=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx" && grep -q 'timeout_s=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)" \
        "plugin.run.timed_out event in lifecycle.sh is missing stage= or timeout_s= field"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"

# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do
    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
    [[ -f "$_file" ]] || continue
    if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' "$_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)" \
            "plugin_hook_call not found — this dispatch route would bypass the watchdog"
    fi
done

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] no hand-rolled TERM/KILL in lifecycle.sh for dispatch ────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # After the change: no `kill -TERM` or `kill -KILL` hand-rolled in
    # plugin_hook_call itself — these are replaced by zbuild_pg_kill.
    # Allow lines that are purely comments.
    _hand_rolled=""
    _hand_rolled="$(grep -E 'kill -TERM|kill -KILL' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hand_rolled" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found: $(printf '%s' "$_hand_rolled" | head -3 | tr '\n' '|') — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill"

_le="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_le" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/orch/local_engine.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' "$_le"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill" \
            "not found — _orch_local_collect_results still has a hand-rolled kill sequence"
    fi

    # The old _orch_local_kill_slot is replaced; if it still exists, that is a bug.
    if grep -q '_orch_local_kill_slot' "$_le"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh" \
            "still present — the hand-rolled kill helper was not replaced by zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── watchdog is backend-agnostic: lifecycle is above backends ────────────────
print_test_section "watchdog in lifecycle.sh is backend-agnostic (above the backend layer)"

# The watchdog's position in lifecycle.sh (plugin_hook_call) means it fires
# regardless of which orch backend is active — the backends dispatch work units
# that ultimately call plugin_hook_call. Verify orch-mock still routes through it.
_mock_plugin="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_mock_plugin" ]]; then
    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # orch-mock dispatches work units that call plugin_hook_call;
    # the backend itself does not arm or disarm the watchdog.
    assert_pass "orch-mock plugin exists (backend-agnostic watchdog can be tested with it)"
fi

# ─── ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence ─────────────────────
print_test_section "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh has no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

_hive="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_hive" ]]; then
    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # The hive plugin must not have a kill -TERM / kill -KILL that would intercept
    # the lifecycle-level watchdog's signal before it reaches the hook subshell.
    # (Pool-management kills in the backend's own shutdown are acceptable.)
    _hive_kills=""
    _hive_kills="$(grep -n 'kill -TERM\|kill -KILL' "$_hive" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hive_kills" ]]; then
        assert_fail "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found kill -TERM/-KILL in ruflo-hive — may suppress lifecycle-level watchdog signal:" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$_hive_kills" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    else
        assert_pass "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-8] Guard: orch-sequential is retired.
#
# After this change:
#   - plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ does not exist on disk
#   - no file outside docs/adr/ names "orch-sequential"
#   - configuring `sequential` as an orchestrator backend makes the run end as
#     `misconfigured`
#
# [#1801/SPEC-11] Guard: ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 have ## Enforced by
# sections and are NOT in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where orch-sequential still exists, where
# code files still reference it, and where the ADRs lack Enforced-by sections)
# and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-8] orch-sequential retired; [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR Enforced-by sections"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] the directory is absent ───────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"

if [[ -e "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent" \
        "directory still exists — the retired backend was not removed"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"

# Directories the guard allows: docs/adr/ (historical references are fine there)
# and tests/golden (the golden for the deleted plugin will also be gone).
# The guard runs via grep -r, excluding those two directories.
_bad_refs=""
while IFS= read -r _match; do
    [[ -z "$_match" ]] && continue
    # Strip repo root prefix for readability
    _rel="${_match#$REPO_ROOT/}"
    _bad_refs+="  $_rel"$'\n'
done < <(grep -rl 'orch-sequential' "$REPO_ROOT" \
    --exclude-dir='.git' \
    --exclude-dir='legacy-DoNotUse' 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/docs/adr/' | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/golden/' | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/unit/orch-sequential-retired-guard-test\.sh$' | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test\.sh$' || true)

if [[ -n "$_bad_refs" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential" \
        "found references:"$'\n'"$_bad_refs"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend → misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as a backend ends the run as misconfigured"

# source contract.sh with a controlled env so _orch_load_backend uses the
# sequential alias and we can capture its outcome.
_orch_result=""
_orch_rc=0
_orch_result="$(
    ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND=sequential \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    bash -c '
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        # After the change, orch_load_backend emits orch.backend.misconfigured
        # or writes a misconfigured disposition; check what the function does.
        orch_load_backend sequential 2>&1
        echo "rc=$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || _orch_rc=$?

# The requirement: configuring sequential emits misconfigured
# Accept either an event name match or an explicit "misconfigured" in output
if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|sequential.*not found|backend.*sequential.*not' <<< "$_orch_result"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured" \
        "output: $(printf '%s' "$_orch_result" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr054="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr054" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 exists" "file not found: $_adr054"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr054"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent — ADR-054 §9 requires it"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr017="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-017-per-stage-router-config.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr017" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 exists" "file not found: $_adr017"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr017"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr011="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr011" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 exists" "file not found: $_adr011"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr011"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] the three ADRs are not in the enforcement baseline ───────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054, ADR-017, ADR-011 removed from adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"

_baseline="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
if [[ ! -f "$_baseline" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt exists" \
        "file not found: $_baseline"
else
    for _adr_name in ADR-054 ADR-017 ADR-011; do
        if grep -q "$_adr_name" "$_baseline"; then
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
                "$_adr_name still listed — remove after adding its Enforced-by section"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
        fi
    done
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
26	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
27	
28	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
29	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
30	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
32	
33	print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
34	setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
35	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
36	
37	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
38	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
39	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
40	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
41	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
42	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"
43	
44	# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
45	# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
46	# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
47	# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
48	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
49	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
50	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
51	cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
52	
53	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
54	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
55	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
56	
57	# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
58	# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
59	# no-op rather than a witness.
60	# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
61	# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
62	# after it. #1850: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's v2 declaration —
63	# result_contract 2 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
64	for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
65	    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
66	    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
67	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
68	id: $_id
69	name: Test $_id
70	kind: $_kind
71	version: 0.0.1
72	hooks:
73	  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
74	  cleanup: $_fn
75	requires:
76	  core:
77	    - redaction
78	provides:
79	  result_contract: 2
80	outputs:
81	  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
82	    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
83	    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
84	    format: json
85	    required: true
86	    primary: true
87	config:
88	  valid_verdicts: [pass, error]
89	EOF
90	done
91	
92	# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
93	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
94	intake_run() {
95	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
96	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
97	    return 0
98	}
99	intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
100	PLUG
101	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
102	build_run() {
103	    : > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
104	    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
105	        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
106	    fi
107	    if [[ "${BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
108	        # Spawn a child that ignores TERM and records its PID — used to verify
109	        # that an external SIGTERM to the runner kills the run hook's process group.
110	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${BUILD_STARTED%/*}/run-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
111	        local _j; for _j in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
112	    fi
113	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
114	    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
115	    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
116	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
117	    else
118	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"error","disposition":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
119	    fi
120	    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
121	}
122	build_cleanup() {
123	    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
124	    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
125	    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
126	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
127	        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
128	        sleep 120
129	    fi
130	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
131	        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
132	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
133	        wait
134	    fi
135	    return 0
136	}
137	PLUG
138	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
139	test_run() {
140	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
141	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
142	    return 0
143	}
144	test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
145	PLUG
146	
147	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
148	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
149	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
150	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
151	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
152	
153	_case_no=0
154	# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
155	_prep() {
156	    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
157	    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
158	    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
159	    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
160	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
161	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
162	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="$CASE_DIR/events/events.db"
163	    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
164	    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
165	    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
166	    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
167	}
168	
169	# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
170	#
171	# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
172	# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
173	# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
174	# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
175	# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
176	# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
177	#
178	# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
179	# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
180	#
181	# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
182	# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
183	# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
184	# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
185	# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
186	# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
187	# returns, which a killed stage never does.
188	_assert_released() {
189	    local _case="$1"; shift
190	    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
191	    local _stage _missing=""
192	    for _stage in "$@"; do
193	        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
194	    done
195	    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
196	        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
197	    else
198	        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
199	            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
200	    fi
201	    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
202	        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
203	    else
204	        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
205	    fi
206	}
207	
208	# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
209	print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
210	_prep success
211	export BUILD_RC=0
212	set +e
213	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
214	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
215	_rc=$?
216	set -e
217	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
218	_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test
219	
220	# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
221	print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
222	_prep nonzero
223	export BUILD_RC=1
224	set +e
225	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
226	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
227	_rc=$?
228	set -e
229	if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
230	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
231	else
232	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
233	fi
234	_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build
235	
236	# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
237	print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
238	_prep sigint
239	export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
240	set +e
241	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
242	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
243	_rc=$?
244	set -e
245	# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
246	# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
247	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
248	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
249	    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
250	_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build
251	
252	# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
253	print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
254	_prep sigterm
255	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
256	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
257	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
258	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
259	    RUNNER_PID=$!
260	else
261	    set -m
262	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
263	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
264	    RUNNER_PID=$!
265	    set +m
266	fi
267	for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
268	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
269	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
270	# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
271	# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
272	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
273	_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build
274	
275	# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
276	# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
277	#
278	# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
279	# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
280	# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
281	# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
282	# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
283	# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
284	# runs could never reproduce.
285	#
286	# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
287	# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
288	# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
289	# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
290	# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
291	print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
292	_prep timeout
293	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
294	_tbin=""
295	if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
296	elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
297	fi
298	if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
299	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
300	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
301	else
302	    # #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own teardown
303	    # budget, not guessed.
304	    #
305	    # The engine bounds each always-run stage by its template `stage_timeout_s`,
306	    # falling back to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) only when the template
307	    # sets none (#2287) — so the pin below is a fallback, and this case relies on
308	    # its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound. Three stages
309	    # release on this path, so an unpinned run is entitled to spend far longer
310	    # tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here. When it did, this
311	    # test SIGKILLed the runner mid-teardown and then asserted on the markers
312	    # teardown had not yet written: the marker came back EMPTY, with BOTH stages
313	    # missing rather than one. Under a loaded machine that is exactly what
314	    # happened, intermittently, for as long as this test has existed.
315	    #
316	    # Pin the budget so the worst case is knowable, then clear it with margin.
317	    # The backstop exists so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite —
318	    # it must never be the thing that stops teardown finishing.
319	    _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=3
320	    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
321	    set -m
322	    ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S="$_SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
323	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
324	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
325	    RUNNER_PID=$!
326	    set +m
327	    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
328	    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
329	    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
330	    _spec5_killer=$!
331	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
332	    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
333	    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
334	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
335	    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
336	fi
337	
338	# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
339	# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
340	# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
341	# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
342	print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
343	_prep blocking
344	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP=1
345	_t0=$(date +%s)
346	set +e
347	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-blocking" ) \
348	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
349	set -e
350	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
351	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP
352	# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
353	# `stage_timeout_s` (30 in the template, which takes precedence over
354	# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S), so the runner returns in about 30s. Allow generous
355	# headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
356	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
357	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
358	else
359	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
360	fi
361	# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
362	# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
363	# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
364	# runner returns; the 1s grace only covers the killed processes exiting on a
365	# loaded host.
366	sleep 1
367	_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
368	if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
369	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
370	elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
371	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
372	    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
373	    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
374	    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
375	    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
376	    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
377	else
378	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
379	fi
380	
381	# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
382	# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
383	# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
384	# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
385	print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
386	# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
387	# case is only about what survives it.
388	_prep blocking-ignore-term
389	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
390	set +e
391	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
392	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
393	set -e
394	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
395	_child_pid=""
396	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
397	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
398	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
399	done
400	_alive=1
401	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
402	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
403	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
404	fi
405	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
406	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
407	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
408	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
409	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
410	else
411	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
412	fi
413	
414	# ── SPEC-2ext [#1801/SPEC-2]: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group
415	# SPEC-2 says: "when the runner is externally killed, its signal handler must
416	# also kill any isolated hook process group". The run hook spawns a child that
417	# ignores TERM. After the runner is externally killed, the child must not survive
418	# because zbuild_pg_kill (or the equivalent KILL sequence) sends SIGKILL to the
419	# entire process group, which the child cannot ignore.
420	print_test_section "SPEC-2ext: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group [#1801/SPEC-2]"
421	_prep sigterm-runpg
422	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM=1
423	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
424	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
425	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
426	    RUNNER_PID=$!
427	else
428	    set -m
429	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
430	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
431	    RUNNER_PID=$!
432	    set +m
433	fi
434	_run_child_pid=""
435	for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
436	    _run_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/run-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
437	    [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
438	done
439	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
440	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
441	unset BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM
442	_alive_run=1
443	if [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
444	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive_run=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
445	fi
446	if [[ -z "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
447	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] fixture: run hook child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/run-child.pid"
448	elif [[ "$_alive_run" -eq 1 ]]; then
449	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)" \
450	        "pid $_run_child_pid still alive — hook process group was not killed when runner received SIGTERM"
451	    kill -KILL "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
452	else
453	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)"
454	fi
455	
456	cleanup_test_env
457	print_test_results
458	exit $((FAIL > 0))
459

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's v2 declaration —
# result_contract 2 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 2
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
config:
  valid_verdicts: [pass, error]
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {
    : > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    if [[ "${BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # Spawn a child that ignores TERM and records its PID — used to verify
        # that an external SIGTERM to the runner kills the run hook's process group.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${BUILD_STARTED%/*}/run-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        local _j; for _j in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"error","disposition":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="$CASE_DIR/events/events.db"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
_prep success
export BUILD_RC=0
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test

# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
_prep nonzero
export BUILD_RC=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
fi
_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build

# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
_prep sigint
export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
else
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
fi
for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build

# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
#
# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
# runs could never reproduce.
#
# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
_prep timeout
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
_tbin=""
if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own teardown
    # budget, not guessed.
    #
    # The engine bounds each always-run stage by its template `stage_timeout_s`,
    # falling back to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) only when the template
    # sets none (#2287) — so the pin below is a fallback, and this case relies on
    # its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound. Three stages
    # release on this path, so an unpinned run is entitled to spend far longer
    # tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here. When it did, this
    # test SIGKILLed the runner mid-teardown and then asserted on the markers
    # teardown had not yet written: the marker came back EMPTY, with BOTH stages
    # missing rather than one. Under a loaded machine that is exactly what
    # happened, intermittently, for as long as this test has existed.
    #
    # Pin the budget so the worst case is knowable, then clear it with margin.
    # The backstop exists so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite —
    # it must never be the thing that stops teardown finishing.
    _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    set -m
    ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S="$_SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
_prep blocking
export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP=1
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-blocking" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
unset BLOCK_CLEANUP
# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
# `stage_timeout_s` (30 in the template, which takes precedence over
# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S), so the runner returns in about 30s. Allow generous
# headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
fi
# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
# runner returns; the 1s grace only covers the killed processes exiting on a
# loaded host.
sleep 1
_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
_prep blocking-ignore-term
export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
set -e
unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# from the template's `always_run:`, resolved by role through the same
    # `resolve_plugin_for_role` seam every dispatch strategy uses.
    #
    # Scope stays pinned to `release` for the teardown role: free live resources
    # and delete NOTHING, so a failed run keeps all of its evidence on disk.
    # `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from any run path.
    _runner_dispatch_always_run() {
        [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" && -f "${_runner_state_file}" ]] || return 0
        [[ "${#_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
        local plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
        local _ar_stage _ar_safe _ar_role _ar_to _ar_dir _ar_guard
        for _ar_stage in "${_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}"; do
            _ar_safe="${_ar_stage//-/_}"
            # Per-stage, not global: the trap can be reached more than once, and
            # there is now more than one always-run stage to keep track of.
            _ar_guard="_RUNNER_AR_DISPATCHED_${_ar_safe}"
            [[ "${!_ar_guard:-0}" == "1" ]] && continue
            printf -v "$_ar_guard" '%s' 1

            local _ar_roles_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_role="${!_ar_roles_var:-}"
            [[ -n "$_ar_role" ]] || continue
            # roles: is a list; an always-run stage takes the first.
            _ar_role="${_ar_role%%,*}"

            _ar_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$_ar_role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [[ -z "$_ar_dir" || ! -d "$_ar_dir" ]]; then
                # LOUD, unlike the old `[[ -d ... ]] || return 0`. An always-run
                # stage that cannot be resolved has not run, and the operator
                # needs to know that rather than infer it from a missing effect.
                eb_emit_event "stage.always_run.unresolved" "stage=$_ar_stage" "role=$_ar_role" 2>/dev/null || true
                continue
            fi

            local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_to="${!_ar_to_var:-}"
            [[ "$_ar_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ar_to" -gt 0 ]] || _ar_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-30}"
            [[ "$_ar_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ar_to" -gt 0 ]] || _ar_to=30

            # Load process-group kill helpers if not already loaded.
            if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi

            # Bounded, because this runs inside the EXIT trap: a hook that blocks
            # would turn a Ctrl-C into a hang — the exact class of bug this
            # mechanism exists to prevent. A timeout BINARY cannot be used here
            # (plugin_hook_call is a shell function; timeout can only exec a
            # command, so the wrapper would fail with "command not found" and
            # silently skip every dispatch). The bound is therefore a watchdog
            # that is CANCELLED on the normal path, so no stray `sleep` outlives
            # the run.
            #
            # `|| true` because an always-run stage's failure is recorded as an
            # event and must NEVER change the run's exit status.
            #
            # #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it.
            # Signalling the one PID reached only the outer shell: the subshell
            # running the stage hooks, and anything it spawned, lived on after
            # the run and wrote into its state minutes later. `set -m` (as the
            # router's model spawn does, #2056) makes each job a process-group
            # leader, so zbuild_pg_kill reaches the whole tree — TERM + 10 s
            # grace + KILL. The watchdog gets its own group too, so cancelling
            # it leaves no `sleep` behind.
            (
                export ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_SCOPE=release
                set -m
                plugin_hook_call "$_ar_dir" run "$_ar_stage" "$_runner_state_file" &
                _ar_pid=$!
                ( set +m; sleep "$_ar_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_ar_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
                _wd_pid=$!
                set +m
                wait "$_ar_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                # #2333: the leader exiting does not mean its group did. A member
                # that ignored TERM would lose its KILL when the watchdog is
                # cancelled below, so KILL the group now; a no-op when it is gone.
                kill -KILL -- -"$_ar_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                kill -TERM -- -"$_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                wait "$_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        done
        return 0
    }

    _runner_abort_trap() {
        # #1829: free live resources first, while the state file and the
        # process tree are still intact.
        _runner_dispatch_always_run
        # #1688: release the issue lock EXPLICITLY. Relying on process death is
        # not enough — a flock belongs to the open file description, which every
        # child inherits, so one lingering child would keep the issue locked
        # after this run is gone. Released after the always-run stages, which
        # still belong to this run.
        if declare -F zbuild_issue_lock_release >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            zbuild_issue_lock_release || true
        fi
        if declare -F zbuild_run_cap_release >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            zbuild_run_cap_release || true
        fi
        # ADR-025 (Wave 15-B #684): the sentinel must be cleared on EVERY
        # exit path — clean end, normal failure, or abort — so a follow-on
        # zbuild invocation in the same state_dir never sees a stale
        # signal. Runs BEFORE the short-circuit because the
        # `_runner_ended=true` path is the common case (every successful
        # run hits it) and that path also needs the cleanup.
        _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel
        # Best-effort: drop THIS run's own lock siblings so a killed run does
        # not leave a stale .lock behind. flock releases on fd close at process
        # death regardless, but the on-disk lock FILE would otherwise linger;
        # this is belt-and-suspenders to the authoritative --no-resume startup
        # clear (the trap may be deferred behind a foreground `wait`, #run-hygiene).
        if [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]]; then
            local _rd; _rd="$(dirname "$_runner_state_file")"
            rm -f "$_runner_state_file.lock" "$_rd/events.jsonl.lock" \
                  "$_rd/events.db.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        # #2131: the normal path — pipeline.end and the always-run stages are
        # on disk; the sidecar renders them in its final PATCH, then goes.
        if [[ "$_runner_ended" == "true" ]]; then _runner_status_comment_reap; return 0; fi
        # Clean teardown (signal/OOM) → interrupted; operator cancel → aborted handled elsewhere.

id: resume-minimal
name: Resume Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# Minimal 3-leaf roster (#1098, PC5): the resume-after-SIGINT contract
# (full-pipeline-sigint resume path, Wave 15-E #685) is NOT stage-count
# dependent — it needs only: a stage BEFORE build (intake) to prove resume
# skips an already-complete stage, the build stage that SIGINTs / re-runs,
# and a stage AFTER build (test) to prove resume continues past build.
# Replaces the full ~14-stage standard roster the test used to register so
# the two real subprocess runs (SIGINT + --resume) drive far fewer dispatch
# units. Linear flow, no cycles (resume logic is the same either way).
#
# #1270: this is a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (extends: simple).
# When merged over the base, the resulting file carries BOTH the base `flow:`
# and this `stages:` list, so the loader treats it as OLD-shape and honors ONLY
# the stages below (the base roster is discarded — it just has to exist).
#
# Stages declare NO `roles:` block on purpose. With roles, the runner routes
# the stage through the fanout strategy (orch pool), which collapses a child
# rc=130 into a generic rc=1 — that would break the SIGINT-propagation
# contract (build returns 130 → runner must exit 130). Without roles, the
# runner resolves the plugin by stage ID and calls plugin_hook_call directly,
# preserving the leaf's exact rc (the same effective dispatch the standard
# template gets via cycle_dispatch_stage for its cycle-member build).
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]
      tail_lines: 200
  - id: build
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]
      tail_lines: 200
    router:
      timeout_s: 900
      max_turns: 0
  - id: test
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]
      tail_lines: 200
