1	id: simple
2	name: Simple Pipeline
3	extends: null
4	
5	# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
6	merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged
7	
8	defaults:
9	  strategy: map
10	
11	# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
13	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
14	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
15	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
16	#
17	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
18	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
19	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
20	# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
21	# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
22	# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
23	#
24	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
25	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
26	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
27	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
28	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
29	# one work unit per lens element — followed by
30	# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
31	# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
32	# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
33	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
34	flow:
35	  - hydrate
36	  - intake
37	  - plan
38	  - delivery_loop
39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
122	  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
123	  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
124	  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
125	  exit_when:
126	    all:
127	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
129	  max_iterations: 2
130	  on_max: halt
131	
132	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
133	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
134	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
135	# party cannot re-author it.
136	spec-coverage:
137	  gate: auto
138	  roles: [spec_coverage]
139	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
140	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
141	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
142	  persona: product-owner
143	  stage_timeout_s: 600
144	  router:
145	    timeout_s: 600
146	
147	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
148	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
149	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
150	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
151	test-author:
152	  gate: auto
153	  roles: [test_author]
154	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
155	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
156	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
157	  blocking: true
158	  stage_timeout_s: 900
159	  router:
160	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
161	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
162	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
163	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
164	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
165	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
166	    timeout_s: 900
167	    max_turns: 0
168	    max_iterations: 4
169	
170	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
171	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
172	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
173	spec-correspondence:
174	  gate: auto
175	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
176	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
177	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
178	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
179	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
180	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
181	  persona: quality-assurance
182	  stage_timeout_s: 600
183	  router:
184	    timeout_s: 600
185	
186	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
187	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
188	assertion-integrity:
189	  gate: auto
190	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
191	  stage_timeout_s: 600
192	
193	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
194	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
195	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
196	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
197	issue-acceptance:
198	  gate: auto
199	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
200	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
201	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
202	  persona: product-owner
203	  stage_timeout_s: 600
204	  router:
205	    timeout_s: 600
206	
207	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
208	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
209	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
210	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
211	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
212	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
213	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
214	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
215	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
216	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
217	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
218	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
219	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
220	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
221	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
222	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
223	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
224	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
225	# which goes round from design.
226	build_test_cycle:
227	  type: cycle
228	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
229	  flow:
230	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
231	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
232	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
233	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
234	    - test-author
235	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
236	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
237	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
238	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
239	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
240	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
241	    - spec-correspondence
242	    - build
243	    - test
244	    - shape-floor
245	    - acceptance-gate
246	    - secret-scan
247	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
248	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
249	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
250	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
251	    # rewritten assertion.
252	    - assertion-integrity
253	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
254	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
255	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
256	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
257	    - issue-acceptance
258	    - gate-aggregator
259	  exit_when:
260	    stage: gate-aggregator
261	    field: verdict
262	    op: eq
263	    value: pass
264	  max_iterations: 3
265	  on_max: continue
266	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
267	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
268	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
269	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
270	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
271	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
272	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
273	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
274	intake:
275	  gate: auto
276	  roles: [intake]
277	  stage_timeout_s: 600
278	  io:
279	    destinations: [file, stdout]
280	    tail_lines: 200
281	
282	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
283	plan:
284	  gate: auto
285	  roles: [planner]
286	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
287	  persona: product-owner
288	  stage_timeout_s: 1200
289	  io:
290	    destinations: [file, stdout]
291	    tail_lines: 200
292	  router:
293	    timeout_s: 300
294	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
295	    # headroom. The planner is
296	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
297	    max_turns: 45
298	
299	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
300	design:
301	  gate: auto
302	  roles: [designer]
303	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
304	  persona: architect
305	  stage_timeout_s: 3900
306	  io:
307	    destinations: [file, stdout]
308	    tail_lines: 200
309	  router:
310	    timeout_s: 600
311	    max_turns: 0
312	
313	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
314	# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
315	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
316	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
317	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
318	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
319	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
320	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
321	design-gate:
322	  gate: auto
323	  roles: [design_gate]
324	  stage_timeout_s: 600
325	  io:
326	    destinations: [file, stdout]
327	    tail_lines: 200
328	
329	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
330	build:
331	  gate: auto
332	  roles: [builder]
333	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
334	  persona: developer
335	  stage_timeout_s: 4200
336	  io:
337	    destinations: [file, stdout]
338	    tail_lines: 200
339	  router:
340	    timeout_s: 900
341	    max_turns: 0
342	
343	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
344	test:
345	  gate: auto
346	  roles: [tester]
347	  stage_timeout_s: 5400
348	  io:
349	    destinations: [file, stdout]
350	    tail_lines: 200
351	
352	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
353	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
354	shape-floor:
355	  gate: auto
356	  roles: [shape_floor]
357	  stage_timeout_s: 600
358	  io:
359	    destinations: [file, stdout]
360	    tail_lines: 200
361	
362	# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
363	# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
364	# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
365	# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
366	# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
367	# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
368	# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
369	# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
370	acceptance-gate:
371	  gate: auto
372	  roles: [acceptance_gate]
373	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
374	  stage_timeout_s: 600
375	  io:
376	    destinations: [file, stdout]
377	    tail_lines: 200
378	  router:
379	    timeout_s: 600
380	    max_turns: 10
381	
382	# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
383	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
384	# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
385	secret-scan:
386	  gate: auto
387	  roles: [secret_scan]
388	  stage_timeout_s: 600
389	  io:
390	    destinations: [file, stdout]
391	    tail_lines: 200
392	
393	# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
394	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
395	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
396	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
397	gate-aggregator:
398	  gate: auto
399	  roles: [gate_aggregator]
400	  stage_timeout_s: 600
401	  io:
402	    destinations: [file, stdout]
403	    tail_lines: 200
404	
405	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
406	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
407	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
408	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
409	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
410	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
411	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
412	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
413	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
414	#
415	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
416	# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
417	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
418	review_lenses:
419	  type: map
420	  over: lenses
421	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
422	  # from the lens's name.
423	  elements:
424	    - id: security
425	      persona: security
426	    - id: performance
427	      persona: performance
428	    - id: red-team
429	      persona: red-team
430	    - id: correctness
431	      persona: correctness
432	    - id: scope
433	      persona: scope
434	    - id: sre
435	      persona: sre
436	  roles: [review_lens]
437	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
438	  max_parallel: 4
439	  on_member_error: continue
440	  aggregate: advisory
441	  stage_timeout_s: 600
442	  io:
443	    destinations: [file]
444	    tail_lines: 200
445	  router:
446	    timeout_s: 300
447	    max_turns: 25
448	
449	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
450	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
451	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
452	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
453	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
454	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
455	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
456	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
457	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
458	review-aggregator:
459	  gate: auto
460	  roles: [review_aggregator]
461	  stage_timeout_s: 600
462	  io:
463	    destinations: [file, stdout]
464	    tail_lines: 200
465	
466	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
467	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
468	pr:
469	  gate: auto
470	  roles: [pr]
471	  stage_timeout_s: 600
472	  io:
473	    destinations: [file, stdout]
474	    tail_lines: 200
475	
476	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
477	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
478	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
479	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
480	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
481	#
482	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
483	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
484	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
485	release:
486	  gate: auto
487	  roles: [teardown]
488	  stage_timeout_s: 30
489	  io:
490	    destinations: [file]
491	    tail_lines: 50
492	
493	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
494	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
495	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
496	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
497	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
498	# abort.
499	#
500	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
501	# process-group kill does not.
502	persist:
503	  gate: auto
504	  roles: [persist]
505	  stage_timeout_s: 120
506	  io:
507	    destinations: [file]
508	    tail_lines: 50
509	
510	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
511	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
512	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
513	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
514	#
515	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
516	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
517	# an earlier push never delivered.
518	hydrate:
519	  gate: auto
520	  roles: [hydrate]
521	  stage_timeout_s: 600
522	  router:
523	    timeout_s: 60
524	  io:
525	    destinations: [file]
526	    tail_lines: 50
527

file.content:
id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  stage_timeout_s: 900
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]
  stage_timeout_s: 600

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 1200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
    # headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  stage_timeout_s: 3900
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  stage_timeout_s: 4200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  stage_timeout_s: 5400
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.

  type: map
  over: lenses

  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  stage_timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  stage_timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# plugins/tool/teardown/plugin.sh — Teardown plugin (ADR-054 §7, issue #1829)
#
# Kind: tool  Tier: T0  (NO LLM calls — NEVER call route_to_model)
# Dispatched by the runner at every pipeline exit path with scope=release.
# Iterates over stages that executed (status=complete or status=failed) from
# pipeline-state.json and calls plugin_hook_call cleanup for each.
# A plugin with no cleanup hook returns 0 and emits `plugin.cleanup.absent`
# (#1823) — nothing to free is not a failure, so it needs no special case here.
# Always exits 0 — teardown failures are events, not verdict changes.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_LOADED=1

# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh"
zbuild_plugin_bootstrap "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/stage-summary.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/stage-summary.sh"
_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_DIR="$_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR"
_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_ROOT="$_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_ROOT"

# shellcheck source=../../../core/event-bus/event-bus.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../../core/plugin-registry/registry.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../../core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
# resolve_stage_plugin lives here; declare it rather than inherit the runner's
# scope — without it any other caller frees nothing and still returns 0.
source "$_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_ROOT/core/pipeline/dispatch.sh"

# ─── teardown_run ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Entry point called by the pipeline engine.
# Usage: teardown_run <stage_id> <state_file>
# Scope is read from ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_SCOPE (default: release).
teardown_run() {
    local _stage_id="${1:-teardown}"
    local _state_file="${2:-}"

    # Fail-safe: an unrecognised scope degrades to `release`, the scope that
    # deletes nothing. The destructive scope is never the fallback.
    local _scope="${ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_SCOPE:-release}"
    case "$_scope" in
        release|purge) ;;
        *)
            emit_event "teardown.scope.invalid" \
                "requested=$_scope" "used=release" 2>/dev/null || true
            _scope="release"
            ;;
    esac
    local _plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_ROOT/plugins}"

    local _state_dir=""
    [[ -n "$_state_file" ]] && _state_dir="$(dirname "$_state_file")"

    # Read stages that executed (complete or failed) from pipeline-state.json.
    local -a _executed=()
    if [[ -n "$_state_file" && -f "$_state_file" ]]; then
        local _s
        while IFS= read -r _s; do
            [[ -n "$_s" ]] && _executed+=("$_s")
        # NB: the durable key is `stage_statuses` and its values are plain
        # strings, not objects. Reading `.stages[].status` (which no state file
        # has ever had) yields an empty list, which makes teardown a silent
        # no-op that still reports success — verified against a real run's
        # pipeline-state.json before this was corrected.
        done < <(jq -r '
            .stage_statuses // {} |
            to_entries[] |
            select(.value == "complete" or .value == "failed") |
            .key
        ' "$_state_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
    fi

    # ADR-062 §2: union in every stage recorded at DISPATCH.
    #
    # stage_statuses is written by _update_stage_status only on complete/failed
    # — after a stage RETURNS. A stage killed mid-flight never returns, so it
    # never appeared above and was never released: the external-signal paths
    # freed `intake` only while `build` was demonstrably running (#1748, #2001).
    #
    # runtime/stages/<stage>.pgid is written by plugin_hook_call at dispatch
    # (ADR-058 §1's declared purpose for runtime/), so it exists for exactly the
    # stages that started, whether or not they finished.
    if [[ -n "$_state_dir" && -d "$_state_dir/runtime/stages" ]]; then
        local _pgf _pgstage _seen
        # BOTH markers (#2024): `.started` is written at dispatch for every
        # stage that began, `.pgid` by whoever spawned a real process group.
        # The union is what covers a stage killed mid-flight — it never reached
        # stage_statuses, and it may never have spawned a group either.
        for _pgf in "$_state_dir"/runtime/stages/*.started "$_state_dir"/runtime/stages/*.pgid; do
            [[ -e "$_pgf" ]] || continue
            _pgstage="$(basename "$(basename "$_pgf" .pgid)" .started)"
            _seen=0
            for _s in "${_executed[@]+"${_executed[@]}"}"; do
                [[ "$_s" == "$_pgstage" ]] && { _seen=1; break; }
            done
            [[ "$_seen" -eq 0 ]] && _executed+=("$_pgstage")
        done
    fi

  \"verdict\": \"$_verdict\",
  \"disposition\": \"complete\",
  \"reason\": \"$_reason\",
  \"data\": {
    \"targets\": $_targets_json
  }

        emit_event "teardown.result.write_failed" \
            "file=$_result_file" "scope=$_scope" 2>/dev/null || true

    # failed cleanup is stated as such rather than inferred from an event.

        "cleaned up scope $_scope" \
        "$(printf -- '- failures: %s\n- detail: %s' "$_any_failed" "${_reason:-none}")"
    emit_event "teardown.complete" \
        "scope=$_scope" "failed=$_any_failed" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Always return 0: cleanup failures are recorded via events, not propagated.
    return 0
}

   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+on$' <<< "$opts_on"; then

        "got: $opts_on"

E2E_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e/events.jsonl"

# Note: under flag-on, `set -m` puts the plugin subshell in its own PGID

    local _i

# Design notes — issue #1801

## What I found

### Build state
Build ran (39 files changed, +317/-540). Three tests still fail:
1. `tests/integration/runner-job-control-abort-test.sh` — T1 `flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell`
2. `tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` — SPEC-6b: child ignoring TERM alive after runner
3. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh` — SPEC-10: `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` still present

### Root cause of failure 1 (job-control T1)
`plugin_hook_call` now runs the hook subshell as `( set +m; source ...; hook_fn ) &`. The `set +m` inside
the subshell means the plugin cannot observe the runner's monitor-mode flag via `$-`. The T1 probe in 
`runner-job-control-abort-test.sh` records `$-` from inside the plugin subshell and expects `m` to be set
when `ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1`. This was always an indirect observable (plugin inheriting runner's state),
and now the plugin subshell explicitly clears monitor mode. Fix: update T1 assertion to use a structural
check on lifecycle.sh/runner.sh (grep for `set -m` in the appropriate branch).

### Root cause of failure 2 (SPEC-6b)
`_runner_dispatch_always_run` arms an OUTER watchdog on `_ar_pid` (the `plugin_hook_call` process).
`plugin_hook_call` arms an INNER watchdog on `_lc_hook_pid` (the hook subshell group). Both fire
after the same timeout. The outer watchdog sends TERM to `plugin_hook_call`'s group; bash exits the
subshell on TERM (no TERM trap). This orphans `_lc_hook_pid`'s inner group (with any TERM-ignoring children),
because `plugin_hook_call` exits before running `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"`. The inner watchdog
fires late (after the runner returned) and kills the group 10s after that. Fix: add a TERM trap in the
`run` hook branch of `plugin_hook_call` that kills `_lc_hook_pid`'s group before exiting.

### Root cause of failure 3 (SPEC-10)
The SPEC-10 test checks `plugin_hook_call` for any non-comment `kill -TERM|kill -KILL`. Line 525 has:
`kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true` — this is the belt-and-suspenders kill after
`wait "$_lc_hook_pid"`. Fix: replace with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1`.

### SPEC-10 and SPEC-6b relationship
SPEC-10 says no hand-rolled kill. SPEC-6b says children ignoring TERM must die. The fix:
1. Replace `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1`
2. Add TERM trap to kill `_lc_hook_pid`'s group immediately when `plugin_hook_call` receives TERM
   (so the outer watchdog killing `plugin_hook_call` still cleans up the inner group)

### Files confirmed changed by build
- core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh (watchdog added, needs TERM trap + zbuild_pg_kill fix)
- core/pipeline/runner.sh (_runner_dispatch_always_run updated)
- core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh (ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT removed)
- core/orch/local_engine.sh (zbuild_pg_kill used)
- core/orch/contract.sh (sequential backend rejected)
- config/templates/simple.yaml (stage_timeout_s values)
- config/event-schema.json (new events registered)
- config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt (ADR-011, ADR-017, ADR-054 removed)
- docs/adr/ADR-054, ADR-017, ADR-011 (## Enforced by sections added)
- plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ (deleted)
- tests/golden/orch-sequential-capabilities.golden (deleted)
- tests/unit/stage-timeout-*.sh (new tests created)
- tests/unit/orch-sequential-retired-guard-test.sh (new)
- tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh (updated)
- tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh (SPEC-6b added)
- plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh (updated)

### Superseded assertions
- `runner-job-control-abort-test.sh` T1 "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell": probed `$-` from
